answer: The help center names two forms that came in with the February 1, 2026 rewrite. Power of attorney form NW-POA-2 replaced the notarized NW-POA-1, which is accepted only if it was signed before that date and only until June 30, 2026. NW-POA-2 can be signed electronically with no notary, except in Georgia, where it must still be notarized. Odometer disclosure statement NW-ODO-2 replaced NW-ODO-1. Other forms appear in current articles (NW-MIL-1, NW-DMG-1, NW-TRD-1, NW-PU-1, NW-LPA-1), but the help center doesn't say when they were introduced, so I can't confirm they are new. Also, some older articles still refer to the replaced forms: 'Broken or replaced odometer' names NW-ODO-1 and 'Selling a family member's car for them' names NW-POA-1.
